definitions.gloss: fresh green leaves; new foliage; verdure
definitions.explanation: The lush green leaves of trees and plants, especially the fresh new leaves that appear in late spring and early summer. A seasonal word associated with the beauty of nature in May and June.

examples.japanese: {青葉|あおば}が{美|うつく}しい。
{木々|きぎ}の{青葉|あおば}が{風|かぜ}に{揺|ゆ}れている。
examples.english: The green leaves on the trees are swaying in the wind.

examples.japanese: {五月|ごがつ}になると{山|やま}は{青葉|あおば}に{覆|おお}われて、{目|め}に{鮮|あざ}やかだ。
examples.english: In May, the mountains are covered with fresh green leaves, vivid to the eye.

notes:
Refers specifically to the fresh, vibrant green foliage of late spring and early summer. Composed of {青|あお} (green/blue) + {葉|ば} (leaf/leaves). A poetic and seasonal word strongly associated with May and June.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {青葉|あおば}の{季節|きせつ}: the season of fresh green leaves
- {青葉|あおば}が{茂|しげ}る: green leaves grow thick
- {青葉|あおば}の{頃|ころ}: around the time of fresh green foliage
- {目|め}に{青葉|あおば}: green leaves pleasing to the eye (from a famous haiku)

CULTURAL NOTE:
In haiku, {青葉|あおば} is a {季語|きご} (seasonal word) for early summer. The famous phrase {目|め}に{青葉|あおば} {山|やま}ほととぎす {初鰹|はつがつお} by {山口素堂|やまぐちそどう} celebrates three seasonal pleasures: green leaves for the eyes, the cuckoo for the ears, and the first bonito for the palate.

RELATED WORDS:
- {新緑|しんりょく}: fresh greenery — similar meaning but more general; also a seasonal word for early summer
- {若葉|わかば}: young leaves — emphasizes the newness of the leaves rather than their color
- {紅葉|こうよう}: autumn foliage — the seasonal counterpart to {青葉|あおば}
